tasks.behavior: Deposits and balances are confirmed by two independent providers, every payment to a watched invoice is found or alerted, and the watched set stays bounded
acceptance: SEC-01, D-15: hosts alternate between the primary and second RPC roles and a role never fails over to the other's hosts, so one provider can't answer both a deposit and its balance check, also after an outage; SEC-02: invoices are created on a chain only once the worker has its cursor (503 network_not_ready), so the first scan can't skip a payment; F122/F123: RescanDepth is 2,000 blocks (15+ minutes on Arc and Tempo), money on a receive address with no booked transfer raises an ALERT and blocks expiry, deposits book in chain order, an empty balanceOf is an error for the ledger, a deposit mined again under a block called final is skipped with an ALERT; SEC-05/L-03: invoices leave the scan 30 days after their settle deadline and a profile has at most 1,000 open invoices; onboarding counts only the profiles it creates against the cap; backend tests cover each; architecture.md, money-safety.md, api.md and openapi.yaml match
notes: 2026-10-11 review fail by reviewer: FAIL: one blocking defect, plus stale docs. BLOCKING: apps/backend/internal/watcher/watcher.go:231 drops an invoice from the scan by settle_deadline alone. A deposit seen just before the cutoff and not yet final stays 'detected' forever: its log is no longer fetched, so it is never confirmed, and its block is canonical, so it is never marked reorged. start() (:207-213) then always returns that block, Scan caps latest at from+scanLimit-1 (:102), and the cursor can never pass from+40,000. The whole chain stops: no later deposit to any invoice or wallet is found. Anyone can trigger it by paying an old invoice's public receive address in the last minutes before settle_deadline+30d on Base or Arbitrum, where finality takes minutes. Reproduced with a go test -overlay scratch test (repo untouched) on Anvil: a deposit is detected, the invoice crosses the window, 3,000 blocks are mined, then a watched invoice is paid. After 30 scans the first row is still 'detected', the cursor is stuck at 4402 (= N+2299), and the new payment is never recorded. Control run with the invoice still watched: both confirmed, cursor 5106. Fix as F072 did for disabled tokens: invoices() also selects invoices with a detected chain_transfers row. Add this scenario as a test. DOCS (must fix, AGENTS.md says update the owning doc): docs/backend/architecture.md:266, :268 and :271, and docs/PROJECT.md R-38, still say 64 blocks. RescanDepth now also sets the wallet first-scan start, which is 2,000 blocks. The pool_test.go:98-99 comment still says a failed second host is replaced by another. VERIFIED OK: (a) host roles by chains.json. base-sepolia and arbitrum-sepolia without keys: P={chain RPC, drpc} S={publicnode}; with keys: P={infura, publicnode} S={chain RPC, drpc}. arc without keys: P={arc.io, blockdaemon} S={drpc, quicknode}; with keys: P={infura, drpc, quicknode} S={arc.io, blockdaemon}. tempo: P={tempo.xyz} S={drpc}. Every role has at least one host because NewRPCs needs 2 or more hosts, and CheckEnabled can still pass on every chain. (c) best() filters by e.second, so no sequence lets one host serve both roles. TestRolesStayOnDifferentHosts fails on the old code. (d) SEC-02: the cursor commits in the same transaction as the first scan, and any payment after the invoice exists is at or above the cursor's finalized block, so it is in range. A chain that is disabled and re-enabled keeps its cursor and catches up from it. (g) tx.Begin on a pgx.Tx is a SAVEPOINT, Rollback goes back to it, Commit releases it, and the scan goes on (the test fails without it). (i) The chain-order, window, cap, onboard and ErrNotWatched tests each fail without their fix. go test ./internal/{chain,watcher,ledger,invoice,balance,profile} ok. Run logs F122-20261011T155452Z-*: 0 FAIL, e2e 2/2.

tasks.behavior: The signer recovers from stuck deploys and nonce gaps, sizes gas per chain, checks its lock before each settlement, and caps the gas one user's invoices can spend
acceptance: R-22, R-30: a deploy takes over a stuck unsaved transaction at the executor's next mined nonce at twice today's fee; a nonce gap with nothing pending and no saved settle is filled with a zero-value self-transfer; a replacement settle uses max(old gas limit, a fresh estimate x 1.2); Tempo settles get at least TempoSettleGasFloor (580,000); the signer checks lock.Held before each intent; SEC-03: a user's invoices get at most SponsoredPerDay (50) signed settlements in 24 hours, then intents wait with a reason and an ALERT; backend tests on Anvil cover each; architecture.md matches
notes: 2026-10-11 review fail by reviewer: FAIL: acceptance says backend tests on Anvil cover each change, but the replacement gas limit has no test. settle.go:263-267 (gas = max(old.Gas(), est+est/5)) can be removed and the full settlement package still passes (mutation run). TestStuckSettleIsReplacedWithAHigherFee (signer_test.go:889) cannot see it, because the old limit already equals the fresh estimate x 1.2. Fix: add an Anvil test where the saved settle's limit is below a fresh estimate x 1.2 (or the estimate grows) and assert the replacement's Gas() >= est*6/5, and that it equals old.Gas() when the estimate reverts. Everything else checks out. Mutations fail their tests for cap, lock, fillGap no-op, fillGap saved check, overStuck and the Tempo floor. go test settlement+watcher pass; backend e2e passes; verify logs 20261011T161538Z are newer than all edits. overStuck and fillGap only displace unsaved deploys or fillers: the queries are scoped to chain and sender and check status 'sent', which is the only status that holds an unmined nonce, since retry only runs after the nonce is used. retry clears signed_at; confirm keeps it; the cap counts across all of a user's profiles and runs before deploy. Non-blocking: (1) the tests call overStuck and fillGap directly, so their call sites (settle.go:122, reconcile.go:110-114) are not covered. (2) overStuck pays 2x today's tip. If the stuck tx is an earlier overStuck deploy and the tip has not risen 10%, geth refuses the replacement (underpriced) until base fee falls. Deploys on that chain fail every 30 s until then; it recovers on its own. (3) On testnets the deployer key is the executor key (packages/contracts/.env.example), so overStuck can drop a forge deploy.sh tx sent while the signer runs. (4) Without the cap, TestSponsoredSettlementsPerUserAreCapped fails only after a 60 s deploy timeout: the fixture's nonces 1..50 raise sign()'s nonce floor. (5) feeToken adds an eth_getCode per settle, plus an eth_call on Tempo. (6) The cap query's cost grows with a user's lifetime invoices (indexed joins, no signed_at index). (7) Retried intents stop counting toward the cap even when a reverted settle spent gas.

tasks.behavior: Check status on the pay page and the invoice page rechecks an invoice on chain without risk to money or RPCs
acceptance: R-55, D-77: POST /v1/invoices/{id}/recheck compares the receive address's finalized on-chain balance with what is recorded and, when more is on chain, asks the worker to rescan that invoice from its creation block; it never signs; one recheck per invoice every 30 s across replicas (429 with Retry-After), a per-process global limit, per-IP at the edge (Q-8); a backend test books a deposit the regular scan missed only after a recheck; the pay page and the invoice page show Check status and its result (unit and e2e)
notes: 2026-10-13 review fail by subagent: FAIL, 2 blockers + 1 acceptance gap. Re-ran: go test -count=1 ./internal/watcher/ ./internal/worker/ ./internal/invoice/ ./internal/httpapi/ all ok; verify logs F130-20261013T134818Z-* passed. (1) Rescans ignore the scan's watch window, so the ledger books money it otherwise never books. watcher.go:280-282 (invoices) drops invoices 30 days after settle_deadline unless a deposit is detected; architecture.md:250 says later money is moved only by the refund authority, from the chain. rescan.go:23-27 and recheck.go:72 have no such filter. Money sent to an aged-out invoice gets recorded and booked by ProcessChain as payer_held, with refund_status=held (process.go:93,131). Once the refund authority moves that money on chain, the held booking never clears. This is also a cheap abuse path: dust sent to old invoices plus Check status re-queues a rescan from creation (34+ rounds x 20 eth_getLogs on Base) and can keep all RescanLimit slots busy. Fix: apply the same filter in Recheck or in the Rescans query. (2) Rescans block the ledger. worker.go:69-76 runs Rescans on the same 2-minute chainCtx before ProcessChain. A rescan step saves nothing until it has read all of its up-to-40,000-block range (rescan.go:76-100), and logsIn's span starts again at MaxRange on every call (rescan.go:106). So with 5 asked invoices (up to ~100 eth_getLogs plus blockAt's ~2*log2(latest) calls each) on a slow or range-capped RPC, the deadline can run out. ProcessChain then fails for every invoice on the chain, and the next round repeats the same work. Fix: run ProcessChain before Rescans, or give Rescans its own shorter deadline. (3) Acceptance says the pay page and the invoice page show Check status (unit and e2e). Only the pay page has an e2e (pay.spec.ts:163); invoice-detail.tsx:219-229 (hidden when settled) has no test. Verified OK: depositsOf/insertDeposits are a pure move and Scan is unchanged (watcher.go:142-211); rescans record only the invoice's own token to its address, decide final vs detected by the finalized block from the same header batch (rescan.go:84-88), use the same insert path and never write chain_cursors; detected rows are revisited by start() and invoices() EXISTS detected; the per-invoice cooldown is atomic across replicas (recheck.go:42-45); the global bucket runs before any DB or RPC work (routes.go:104); RPC errors are redacted (recheck.go:60, worker.go:74); the API matches openapi.yaml and api.md; the TestRecheckBooksADepositTheScanMissed path holds. Non-blocking: Rescans returns on the first error, so one failing invoice holds up those behind it (rescan.go:47-53); an Arc native payment keeps onChain > recorded forever, so every Check status after a rescan finishes starts a new full rescan; a 429 shows the 'could not reach the network' text (check-status.tsx:44).

Arc repeat: recheck.go:71-78 asks for a new rescan only when none finished within RescanAgainAfter (10 min); tested in TestRecheckInvoice (invoices_recheck_test.go:61-71). A 429 now shows recheckTooSoon (check-status.tsx:47). Earlier checks still hold: the money path is the same as Scan's, the cursor is never written, the cooldown is atomic, the global bucket runs first, errors are redacted, and the API matches the docs. Non-blocking: for an invoice past the watch window, the api still answers rescanning=true ('Recording it now') and the worker then drops the request, so the message is wrong once (recheck.go:78 does not know the window); and a rescan step that times out loses its blockAt result, so it is computed again the next round.

notes: 2026-10-13 review pass by reviewer: Checked the diff c26fe34..a6bb349 for money safety. Ledger: the option row is locked first, then the main row, and chosen_id is set in the same transaction before any booking, so only the chosen option can book to recipient_payable, reach paid or get a settlement intent; deposits on any other option go to payer_held. No lock cycle: Process locks at most its own row then the main row, the main row's own run locks only itself, and the worker runs watcher and ledger in sequence. Triggers: options must share profile, recipient, factory, expiry, settle deadline, key and request hash with a main row that has no choice yet; no option of an option; chosen_id is set once, only on a main row, only to its own options; terms stay fixed by invoices_guard. Reads: every FROM/JOIN invoices in internal/ was checked; get, list, search, activity, recheck, PDFs and settlement wait use invoices_current or the option id; balance, watcher, signer and rescan work per row as intended. Idempotency: rational USD hash is canonical (12.5 = 12.50), partial unique indexes, the constraint name in Create matches the new index. Limits count each option. Canary: fixed invoices still match id, terms, predict on both RPCs and the page; the docs query matches the 10-field parser. Non-blocking: held money on a non-chosen option is not shown on the invoice page or its refund status (only balance and activity); a reorged first transfer keeps the choice (documented); the pay page check now binds the address to optionId from the API, not to the link id; recheck fails with 503 if any one option's chain RPC is down; the invoices_options trigger would let an option be added to a fixed invoice that already has money (no app path does this); a misplaced JSDoc line above InvoiceOption in invoices.ts and an unfinished sentence in canary_test.go. Ran: go test for invoice, ledger, database, canary, httpapi, settlement, activity, document, watcher, balance (all ok); vitest src/features/pay and src/features/invoices (31 passed); check-docs (0 errors).

2026-10-13 review pass by reviewer: Follow-up d1a2e89 (diff a6bb349..d1a2e89). Further options now get id keccak256(abi.encode(first id, chain id, token)); the first stays random. Go (address.OptionID: id, chain id as a big-endian uint256 word, token left-padded to 32 bytes) and TS (optionIdOf: fixedBytes 32, uint, fixedBytes 20 left-padded, lowercased) encode the same 96 bytes, and both tests check the same vector. Another invoice cannot pass under a link: a derived id commits to the link id, so matching would need a keccak collision, and the server picks the random first id. Ids stay unique per invoice because (chain, token) is unique. The pay page accepts optionId only when it equals the link id or derives from it, so fixed invoices keep the old tie. Nothing else changed in behavior: the ledger, triggers, reads and canary logic are untouched; the e2e fixture, api.md and money-safety.md match; the three comment fixes are correct. Note: options made by a6bb349 with random ids would now fail the page check, but that commit was never merged, so no such rows exist outside local data. Earlier non-blocking notes still apply (held money on a non-chosen option is not shown on the invoice page; recheck fails if one option's chain RPC is down; the trigger would allow an option on a fixed invoice that already has money). Ran: go test ./internal/address/ ./internal/invoice/ ./internal/canary/ (ok); vitest src/features/pay (17 passed).
